title: The Sky-Chamber Where Opposites Become Weather

features.name: ascending-descent
features.desc-on-touch: You touch a tower that rises and falls in the same moment, each direction equally true. The contradiction holds perfectly still.

features.name: storm-made-still
features.desc-on-touch: Lightning frozen mid-strike, holding its brightness without moving. The sky holds both the moment before and after the strike.

features.name: breathing-grid
features.desc-on-touch: A grid that expands and contracts like lungs, each square holding a different sky. All the skies are real.

features.name: echo-that-arrives-first
features.desc-on-touch: A sound you hear before it is made. The contradiction doesn't trouble it; they are the same thing arriving from opposite directions.

features.name: reflection-without-mirror
features.desc-on-touch: You see yourself in the air. There is no surface. The sky itself is learning to show back what it receives.

inscription: the sky holds two weathers at once; here they teach each other; neither one cancels the truth of the other

file.name: Weather_Contrapositive_Study_NovDec.txt
file.note: meteorological notes comparing simultaneous opposing front movements; file corrupted to show both outcomes in single grid; both forecasts accurate

exits.label: downward to the hall where truth still doubts itself
further skyward where clouds learn to argue
into dusk where both suns set at once
toward dawn still carrying the night
